title: Memory-Mapped GPIO
constraints: Register map: 0 `OUT` (read/write, drives `gpio_out`), 1 `DIR` (read/write, drives `gpio_oe`), 2 `IN` (read-only), 3 `RISE` (sticky rising-edge flags, write-1-to-clear).
`gpio_in` is asynchronous: pass it through a **2-flop synchronizer**. `IN` reads the output of the second flop.

A third flop holds the previous synchronized value. Every edge where synchronized bit i is 1 and its previous value is 0 sets `RISE[i]`. A write to address 3 clears the bits written as 1. If a bit is set and cleared on the same edge, **set wins**.
`rdata` = the register at `addr`, combinational. Writes to address 2 are ignored. Synchronous reset clears every register and flop.
hints: Pipeline: `s1 <= gpio_in; s2 <= s1; s3 <= s2;` gives `IN = s2` and `rise = s2 & ~s3`.
The sticky flag means software can't miss a short pulse even when it polls slowly.

examples.title: w1c
examples.input: pulse on gpio_in[3], then write 0x08 to RISE
